newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-DAY NINE SNIPPETS FROM WIMBLEDON.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-DAY NINE SNIPPETS FROM WIMBLEDON.

text.p: Day nine snippets from the Wimbledon championships:
Quote of the day - Boris Becker of young German Nicolas Kiefer, whom he has helped train. "It's funny to be in the quarter-finals with one of my pupils."
Stat of the day - 0. Mary-Joe Fernandez's fourth round exit leaves the championship with no American woman in the quarter-finals for the first time since 1946.
Last Eight Baby - Anna Kournikova, 16 last month and the youngest quarter-finalist, was just one year old when her fourth round opponent Helena Sukova first played at Wimbledon.

Enduring appeal - Rain may stop the tennis, but it cannot drive away the fans. Well over a quarter of a million have poured through the gates in the first nine days of the Championships, despite two days lost to rain. The official attendance figure after Tuesday's count was 292,795, a 36,529 increase on last year's figure. This year, however, the All England Club opened for play on Sunday when over 30,000 flocked in.

Ace men - Britain's Greg Rusedski has slammed down 109 aces in his four matches so far. Defending champion Richard Krajicek, whose fourth round match against Tim Henman was suspended for bad light after three sets, has hit 95.
